summary: Terraforming Mars has each player run a corporation drafting and playing project cards to raise Mars's temperature, oxygen, and oceans while building out their own tableau of tags and production. Most of the game is parallel tableau-building, punctuated by competition for shared milestones, awards, and increasingly scarce global-parameter and tile-placement bonuses.
praised: huge variety of cards giving strong replayability
satisfying feeling of building an engine that snowballs
criticised: long playtime with real downtime, especially at higher player counts
card draw luck and uneven card/corporation balance
can feel more solitaire than interactive

interaction.kind: shared board race, mostly parallel tableau building
interaction.detail: Players affect each other by racing to claim milestones and awards and by placing tiles on a shared Mars map for adjacency bonuses, but each player's card tableau and production engine is entirely their own.

scoring.why: Final score sums terraforming contribution, milestones, awards, tile placement, and card-specific victory points, so no single track guarantees the win.
scoring.how_you_win: You win by building the most efficient card engine while also grabbing enough milestones and awards to edge out rivals on the final tally.
